title: Mastery of Entropion: From Diagnosis to Reconstruction
summary: Entropion is the inward turning of the eyelid margin, leading to ocular surface irritation and potential sight-threatening complications. This guide provides a comprehensive clinical framework for managing both involutional and cicatricial subtypes.

sections.title: Definition & Clinical Overview
sections.content: Entropion is defined as the inward rotation of the eyelid margin against the globe. This leads to trichiasis (misdirected lashes) and subsequent mechanical corneal abrasion, epithelial defects, and ulceration. Clinically significant in the elderly due to involutional changes.

rows: Horizontal lid laxity, disinsertion of lower lid retractors, preseptal orbicularis override.
Subconjunctival fibrosis (e.g., OCP, Trachoma, chemical burns) pulling the margin inward.
Ocular irritation leading to orbicularis oculi hyper-contraction.
Rare; often due to developmental abnormalities of the tarsus or lower lid retractors.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Slit-lamp exam to assess degree of corneal staining (Fluorescein).
Step 2: Evert the eyelid to rule out underlying conjunctival scarring.
Step 3: Perform 'Snap-back' test to evaluate horizontal laxity.
Step 4: Distraction test (pull lid >6mm from globe indicates laxity).
Step 5: Inspect lower lid retractors (observe lid position on downgaze).

sections.title: Red Flags (Emergency Signs)
content: Severe conjunctival inflammation suggesting OCP (Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid).

sections.title: Involutional Entropion Correction
content: Quickert sutures: Trans-tarsal full-thickness sutures (absorbable) to reform the retractor-tarsal attachment.
Horizontal Shortening (Lateral Tarsal Strip): Gold standard for severe laxity; lateral canthotomy and strip fixation to the periosteum.
Jones Retractor Reattachment: Direct fixation of the capsulopalpebral fascia to the inferior tarsal border.
Wies Procedure: Transverse eyelid split and everting sutures.

content.explanation: L: Laxity of horizontal lid, A: Attenuation of retractors, X: X-fibrosis (scarring), I: Inferior rectus position, T: Tarsal instability, Y: Yields poor lid apposition.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Never perform a simple wedge resection for involutional entropion as it can worsen the laxity.
Always evaluate the conjunctiva for 'cicatrization' (e.g., symblepharon) before planning surgery; cicatrix requires release, not just tightening.
Botulinum toxin can be a bridge for acute spastic entropion while the ocular surface heals.
Follow-up: Patients must be monitored for recurrence, which occurs in ~5-10% of cases within 5 years.
